newsitem.title: GREECE: EIB sets debt issuance of up to 200 bln drachma.
newsitem.headline: EIB sets debt issuance of up to 200 bln drachma.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) said on Thursday it had signed an accord with state NIBID bank, and other participating banks to set up a drachma debt issuance programme (DIP) of up to 200 billion drachma.
"The EIB finalised today in Athens arrangements for the first ever Greek drachma debt issuance programme (DIP)," it said in a statement.

"Documentation for the up to 200 billion drachma programme was signed by EIB Vice-President, Panayiotis Yennimatas, and NIBID managing director, Dimitris Pavlakis, as well as representatives of the participating banks," it said.

The new facility provides for a wide variety of funding instruments, including fixed-rate, floating-rate and zero-coupon issues and will contribute to the development of the Greek capital market, it added.
"The programme is subject to reverse equity, so that other financial institutions, including institutional investors, may equally join later on," it said.
The EIB lent 721 million ecus to Greece in 1996 and has currently four bond issues outstanding in the drachma market maturing in March 1999 and 2000, it added.
